agentflow-label-text.comment: One or more characters other than brackets, parentheses, braces, vertical bar and double quote are a text-run; agentflow inserts its label comment rule before text-run. flowchart.md#the-label-context: So a label ends at the first `]`, `)`, `}`, or `|` outside a string, and which closing unit the lexer reads depends on the character after it: `A[x])` reads `])`, which does not close a rectangle, and is rejected. agentflow.md#vertices-shapes-and-labels: A property rectangle has two Identifier operands.

agentflow-name.comment: Heading data follows the name or title immediately; a diagram comment ends a bare name heading and is not another name fragment. Ordinary quotes inside a fragment remain text. agentflow.md#flows-globals-connectors-and-names: A diagram comment ends a bare name heading; it is not another name fragment.

agentflow-data-html-tag.comment: A quote outside an HTML attribute starts a data string. changes attribute quotes only; the data closer still ends the block inside a tag or quoted attribute value. agentflow-slanted-html-tag.comment: Converts attribute quotes to single quotes, including after a slash or backslash that starts a new text unit. A converted quote does not protect the slanted closer; the enclosing ordinary run continues after the tag. The attribute part ends at the first >. Read a directive whole; one containing > ends the tag after that directive. agentflow.md#label-and-closing-brace-differences: Reuse flowchart's slanted closer units, including ?] and =] only when reached at a unit position. flowchart.md#the-slanted-context: Rule 5 reads a `/` or `\` as a text run of its own, so a unit can start at a `?` or `=`: `A[/a/?]` is a trapezoid with the label `a/`, while `A[/a?]` is rejected, because the text run `a?` takes the `?`. common.md#html-attribute-quotes: The attribute part may span lines, and it ends at the first `>`. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

patterns.comment: A slash or backslash inside a converted HTML attribute leaves its closing quote as ordinary label text, while a slanted closer still ends the label. flowchart.md#the-slanted-context: Rule 5 reads a `/` or `\` as a text run of its own, so a unit can start at a `?` or `=`: `A[/a/?]` is a trapezoid with the label `a/`, while `A[/a?]` is rejected, because the text run `a?` takes the `?`.
